source_title: Bobby Wright, ‘McHale’s Navy’ Actor, Singer and Son of Kitty Wells, Dies at 84
source_excerpt:
Bobby Wright, the singer and son of country music legend Kitty Wells who played the radio operator Willy Moss on the popular ABC comedy McHale’s Navy , died Tuesday at his home in Madison, Tennessee, his family announced . He was 84.
McHale’s Navy , starring Ernest Borgnine , Joe Flynn and Tim Conway , aired for four seasons (1962-66), and Wright appeared on all 138 episodes of the show that was set on the U.S. Navy boat PT-73 in the Pacific during World War II.
He also appeared with the rest of the cast in the features McHale’s Navy (1964) and McHale’s Navy Joins the Air Force (1966). Related Stories TV Toukie Smith, Top Runway Model and '227' Actress, Dies at 74 Movies Donnie Dunagan, Original Voice of Bambi, Dies at 92

Wright recorded for Decca, ABC and United Artists Records from 1967-79 and had 21 singles on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart, with the gentle “Here I Go Again” peaking at No. 13 in 1971.
His other singles included “Lay Some Happiness on Me,” “Everybody Needs a Rainbow,” a cover of Terry Jacks’ “Seasons in the Sun,” “Lovin’ Someone on My Mind” and “I’m Turning You Loose.”
One of three kids, John Robert Wright Jr. was born on March 30, 1942, in Charleston, West Virginia. His father was Johnnie Wright, who toured the South in an act called Johnnie & Jack, with Wells often performing with them.
At age 8, he sang with his parents on the country music program Louisiana Hayride out of Shreveport and played guitar.
He and his family moved to Nashville in 1958 when his folks became headliners at the Grand Ole Opry, and he graduated from Madison High School, where he played baseball, basketball and football.
Wright came to Hollywood to audition for director Peter Tewksbury ( Father Knows Best , My Three Sons ) for a role on television as a Southern youngster who could play the guitar. The show didn’t move forward, but his screen test was seen by a producer on McHale’s Navy (he was billed as John Wright on the show).
While the comedy was still in production, he gave music another try and worked with his mom on one of her 1965 albums.
After McHale’s Navy ended, Wright played a robber on a 1966 episode of CBS’ Pistols ’n’ Petticoats , a short-lived Western that starred Anne Sheridan, and showed up in the 1974 film Catch the Black Sunshine , starring Ted Cassidy and Chris Robinson .
Wright, who also played bass, trumpet and drums, appeared with his parents and sisters, Ruby and Carol Sue, on the syndicated Kitty Wells Johnnie Wright Family Show for years and toured with his parents until they retired from the road in 2007.
Survivors include Carol Sue; his children, LeAnn and Kamela; his grandchildren, Austin, Cassidy, Shelby and Dalton; his great-grandchildren, Hayden, Pazlee, Remi, Fletcher and Axel; his nieces and nephews, Kitty, John Jr., David, Corrie and Stephanie; and his former wife, Brenda.
Wells, a member of the Country Music Hall of Fame, was country’s first female superstar, racking up nearly three dozen Top 10 hits from 1952-65, including the No. 1 smash “It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels.”

एबीसी कॉमेडी 'मैकहेल्स नेवी' में रेडियो ऑपरेटर विली मॉस की भूमिका निभाने वाले और देश संगीत गायक बॉबी Wright का 84 वर्ष की आयु में निधन हो गया है। उनके परिवार द्वारा की गई घोषणा के अनुसार, राइट का मंगलवार को मैडिसन, टेनेसी स्थित उनके आवास पर निधन हुआ।

30 मार्च 1942 को चार्ल्सटन, पश्चिम वर्जीनिया में जन्मे जॉन रॉबर्ट राइट जूनियर, देश संगीत के दिग्गज कलाकारों किटी वेल्स और जॉनी राइट के पुत्र थे। उन्होंने कम उम्र में ही प्रदर्शन करना शुरू कर दिया था, और 8 वर्ष की आयु में 'लुइसियाना हेराइड' कार्यक्रम में गिटार बजाया तथा गाना गाया।

## टेलीविजन और फिल्म करियर
* अर्नेस्ट बोर्गनाइन, जो फ्लिन और टिम कॉनवे के साथ 'मैकहेल्स नेवी' (1962-1966) के सभी 138 एपिसोड में नजर आए।
* फीचर फिल्मों 'मैकहेल्स नेवी' (1964) और 'मैकहेल्स नेवी जोइन्स द एयर फोर्स' (1966) में अभिनय किया।
* 'पिस्टोल्स एन पेटिकोट्स' जैसे टेलीविजन शो में अतिथि भूमिका निभाई और 1974 की फिल्म 'कैच द ब्लैक सनशाइन' में दिखाई दिए।

## संगीत संबंधी उपलब्धियां
* 1967 से 1979 के बीच डेका, एबीसी और यूनाइटेड आर्टिस्ट्स रिकॉर्ड्स के लिए रिकॉर्डिंग की।
* बिलबोर्ड के हॉट कंट्री सॉन्ग्स चार्ट पर 21 एकल गीत दिए, जिनमें 1971 का उनका एकल गीत "हियर आई गो अगेन" 13वें स्थान पर रहा।
* अपने माता-पिता और बहनों के साथ 'किटी वेल्स जॉनी राइट फैमिली शो' में वर्षों तक टूर किया, जब तक कि उनके माता-पिता ने 2007 में टूरिंग से संन्यास नहीं ले लिया।

राइट के परिवार में उनकी बहन कैरोल सू, उनके बच्चे, पोते-पोतियां, परपोते-परपोतियां और भतीजे-भतीजियां शामिल हैं। उनके निधन की आधिकारिक जानकारी उनके परिवार द्वारा साझा की गई थी।

en_body:
Bobby Wright, known for his role as radio operator Willy Moss on the ABC comedy 'McHale’s Navy' and as a country music singer, has died at the age of 84. According to an announcement by his family, Wright passed away on Tuesday at his home in Madison, Tennessee.

Born John Robert Wright Jr. on March 30, 1942, in Charleston, West Virginia, he was the son of country music legends Kitty Wells and Johnnie Wright. He began performing early in life, singing and playing guitar on the 'Louisiana Hayride' program at age 8 and later moving to Nashville with his family in 1958.

## Television and Film Career
* Appeared in all 138 episodes of 'McHale’s Navy' (1962–1966) alongside Ernest Borgnine, Joe Flynn, and Tim Conway.
* Acted in the feature films 'McHale’s Navy' (1964) and 'McHale’s Navy Joins the Air Force' (1966).
* Guest-starred in television shows including 'Pistols ’n’ Petticoats' and appeared in the 1974 film 'Catch the Black Sunshine'.

## Musical Achievements
* Recorded for Decca, ABC, and United Artists Records between 1967 and 1979.
* Placed 21 singles on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart, with his 1971 single "Here I Go Again" peaking at No. 13.
* Toured for years with his parents and sisters on the 'Kitty Wells Johnnie Wright Family Show' until his parents retired from touring in 2007.

Wright is survived by his family, including his sister Carol Sue, his children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and nieces and nephews. Official details regarding his passing were shared directly by his family.
